55. Mr. Hossain then refers to section 5(3) of the Land Reform Ordinance, 1984 (Ordinance, 1984) and submits that if any property is registered in the name of any person, it shall be presumed that such person is the real owner of the property. In the present case all the confiscated properties were in the names of accused 2 and 4, and the prosecution failed to rebut the presumption of their ownership over the said properties. The learned trial Judge under misconception of law shifted the onus of proof on the appellant and most illegally held him guilty. In order to substantiate his submission on this point, Mr. Hossain refers to S N Kabir vs Fatema Begum and others 66 DLR (AD) 193 and Jay Dayal Poddar (deceased) through L. Rs and another vs Mst. Bibi Hazra and others, AIR 1974 SC 171. 

 60. Mr. Khan, referring to State vs Faisal Morshed Khan and another 66 DLR (AD) 236 further submits that it has already been settled by our Appellate Division that "there may be a situation when there is no assessment of valuation by any competent authority of the Government exercising power on that behalf and in such a case, the Anti-Corruption Commission has no other option but to take the assistance of the PWD officials in making assessment of the valuation of any property. Therefore, it cannot be said that the assessment of valuation made by the PWD officials does not have any evidentiary value in all situations." In the present case the ACC satisfactorily projected and established that the appellant was holding/possessing property in the name of his wife and son, which was beyond his known source of income. Now the onus of proof is squarely on him (appellant) to rebut the presumption of guilt under section 27 (2) of the Act V of the 2004 read with section 7(1) of the Act XL of 1958. But he failed even to show that the property disclosed in the revised statement was consistent to his known source of income. Referring to the evidence of DW 1 Mr. Khan further submits that when accused 1 admits that he himself purchased the apartment at Gulshan and the Mercedes Benz car for his wife, the question of shifting its ownership to accused 2 does not arise. This contention gets support also from the conduct of the co-accused themselves. Their properties were confiscated long back in 2007, but they have not preferred any appeal against the judgment and order, so far it relates to confiscation of their properties, whereas the trial was held in their presence. 

 62. Mr. Nazibur Rahman, learned Deputy Attorney General appearing for the State adopts the submissions advanced by Mr. Khan and supplements that in a case under section 27 of the Act V of 2004, the duty of ACC is only to raise a believable allegation of holding property against a person, which is disproportionate to his known/legal source of income and acquired by illegal means. After bringing such allegation and framing of charge thereon by the Court, if the person fails to prove the contrary, he would be liable for commission of the offence. In the present case, the appellant hopelessly failed to prove contrary to the presumption of guilt that was established against him under section 27 (2) of the Act V of 2004 read with section 7 (1) of the Act XL of 1958. The trial Judge rightly convicted and sentenced him and there is nothing wrong to interfere with.
